This study examines the off-center circular motion of a charged particle within a uniform magnetic field under the influence of the quantum Zener effect. By employing the WKB approximation, we derive analytical formulas for the particle's position and momentum as well as its kinetic energy. Furthermore, we analyze the kinetic energy's dependence on specific parameters and demonstrate that its variation exhibits a novel characteristic: it decreases monotonically as the off-center parameter increases.

We establish a non, local elliptic equation defined on a compact, smooth surface $M$ that features a singular kernel with exponent $\alpha \in (0,1)$. This problem incorporates the critical Sobolev constant and admits solutions that exhibit singular behavior at a single point. The proof relies on analyzing the corresponding operator's spectral properties and investigating the structure of its positive eigenfunctions.

Accurate trajectory prediction for autonomous vehicles is essential for making safe navigation decisions. While current methods typically focus on single-object forecasting, real-world scenarios often involve multiple interacting targets. This paper introduces an innovative simulation-based approach to estimate simultaneous paths for several objects. By utilizing a backward simulation technique, the method generates a comprehensive distribution of potential trajectories for all targets at once. This distribution is subsequently discretized into a fixed number of representative paths, which are subsequently refined through a refinement process to enhance predictive accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods in both trajectory prediction and the selection of appropriate future paths.

This paper introduces a new method for assessing the stability of multi-infeed grid-connected voltage source converters (VSCs) by utilizing a power system admittance matrix model. The approach relies on a linearized model of the VSC control system, which is derived from the original nonlinear formulation. This linearization is achieved by applying a Taylor series expansion to the power system equations, resulting in a state-space representation that is subsequently transformed into an admittance matrix form. The study demonstrates that this derived admittance matrix accurately reflects the dynamic behavior of the VSC. Furthermore, the paper examines the conditions under which the system dynamics remain consistent with the linearized model. Finally, the proposed method's effectiveness is validated through comparative stability analyses of a two-infeed VSC system, utilizing both the new approach and the traditional generalized impedances matrix (GIM) method.

This study examines the characteristics of online signature templates, focusing on the repeatability of specific stroke patterns. We introduce a new metric called "uniqueness," which quantifies the complexity of these templates. By applying this metric to a dataset of 1,000 signatures, we demonstrate that the uniqueness metric effectively distinguishes between different signatures. Furthermore, our findings indicate that the distribution of signature complexity adheres to a Pareto distribution.

In this paper, we examine two distinct geometric frameworks for Hardy sums, defined as $H_{p,q}(n) = \sum_{m_1+\dots+m_q \leq n} m_1 \dots m_q$. First, we establish that these sums correspond to the volumes of specific polyhedra. Second, we demonstrate that they represent the count of integer lattice points located within certain simplices.

We introduce a novel architecture for multi-process operating systems that leverages a stack of persistent memory layers to model the contextual states of various processes. This design facilitates the orchestration of processes across extended timeframes and permits the selective reactivation of specific process instances from their historical contexts. By integrating this framework with a task graph structure, we enable the definition of workflows that are resilient to failures and capable of asynchronous execution.

This study introduces a new approach for estimating human pose in videos, which integrates dilated convolutions with an attention mechanism to enhance the network's receptive field. The method utilizes a 3D ResNet backbone to extract features from video frames, which are subsequently processed by a graph convolutional network (GCN) to model the spatial relationships between body joints. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed framework outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

The CZTI instrument aboard the Indian AstroSat satellite features four segmented detectors, each with a 10° field of view, covering a combined 160° diameter. Although it is primarily designed for X-ray observations of the Earth's vicinity, its capability to detect Earth occultations allows for the analysis of off-axis sources, making it a valuable tool for monitoring celestial objects outside its immediate focus. This study introduces a novel method to utilize this occultation data to derive precise, time-resolved all-sky X-ray light curves. The approach involves analyzing the timing of X-ray flux variations as the Earth blocks and unblocks the CZTI's view of a source. By examining these changes in flux at both the start and end of an occultation, researchers can calculate the source's flux at any given time, even when it is not directly aligned with the detector. The method's accuracy is validated using data from Swift/BAT, XMM-Newton, and Chandra, demonstrating its effectiveness in measuring the light curves of various sources.

Blockchain technology has gained significant traction in recent years, particularly within the cryptocurrency sector. This paper examines the efficiency of blockchain protocols, specifically those used by Bitcoin and Ethereum, by modeling them as distributed systems that operate under a partially synchronous environment. We introduce a new protocol, named "ByzCoin," which is proven to be more efficient than both Bitcoin and Ethereum. Our analysis demonstrates that ByzCoin achieves an optimal message complexity of $O(n)$ per round, whereas Bitcoin and Ethereum incur complexities of $O(n^2)$ and $O(n\log n)$, respectively. Additionally, we prove that Bitcoin and Ethereum fail to match ByzCoin's efficiency, whereas they remain secure against attacks.

Using an effective Hamiltonian that incorporates an enhanced chromomagnetic interaction, we investigate the mass spectra of doubly heavy tetraquarks ($QQ\bar{q}\bar{q}$) with quantum numbers $J^P=1^+$ and $0^+$. Our results indicate that the chromomagnetic interaction significantly influences the mass splitting between the $0^+$ and $1^+$ states. Furthermore, we determine that the doubly heavy tetraquarks $T_{bb}^+$ and $T_{bc}^+$ are likely bound states, whereas $T_{cc}^+$ likely exists as a resonant state.

We demonstrate that the current experimental constraints on neutrinoless double beta decay, combined with the observed near-degeneracy of Higgs boson mass and the top quark mass, necessitate that the electrosymmetry vacuum is unstable. Consequently, the search for vacuum stability becomes an immediate priority, as it may provide a direct test of vacuum metastability. Furthermore, this analysis suggests that the upcoming High-Luminosity LHC run will likely be able to detect deviations from the Standard Model indicative of vacuum instability, provided these effects exceed approximately 10% of the Higgs boson mass.

This paper demonstrates the equivalence between a $q$-logarithmic Sobolev inequality and a $q$-Poincaré inequality within any Carnot structure, and subsequently establishes a link between a $q$-logarithmic Sobolev inequality and a $q$-transport inequality of order 2 on said structure.

This study investigates the application of information geometry within parametric statistical inference, specifically targeting the development of new divergence measures. By utilizing Tomizawa's framework for minimal Bregman divergences, we examine those that are invariant under reparametrization. Our analysis reveals that these invariants are closely linked to the matrix representing the Fisher information. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a reparametrization-invariant Bregman divergence can be derived from a Fisher matrix inverse that corresponds to the covariance structure of the sufficient statistics.

This paper introduces a novel approach to reconstructing 3D geometry and rendering dynamic scenes from sparse sequences of uncalibrated, real-world monocular images. By leveraging a hybrid of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and Signed Distance Functions (SDFs), the method utilizes a multi-stage pipeline. First, it employs a specialized variant of SuperPoint and SuperGlue for robust, efficient feature extraction and matching. Next, it utilizes a multi-view stereo (MVS) network to generate precise 3D point clouds. Finally, these point clouds are integrated with NeRF to synthesize novel views. Experimental results demonstrate that this technique effectively handles real-world dynamic environments, delivering high-quality view synthesis and accurate 3D geometry.

This paper investigates a spectral statistic in quantum graphs, specifically a QKAI-derived quantity, by evaluating it against sums involving periodic orbits without enforcing a semiclassical limit. The findings indicate that these spectral statistics are effectively governed by the sum of periodic orbits, with the relationship becoming explicitly semiclassical only when the parameter $k$ is sufficiently large.

This study introduces a novel technique for determining the periods of variable stars, which is particularly effective for stars exhibiting irregular light variations. The method's performance was evaluated using a simulated dataset of 1,000 stars, where 500 were assigned to a test group and 500 served as a reference group. The test group's light curves were generated by adding irregular variations to the light curves of the reference stars. The new method identified the periods of the 500 test stars with an average accuracy of 0.0001 days, a precision comparable to that of the reference stars. The method's robustness was further confirmed by its successful application to the real-world data of the irregular variable star V1055 Cygni.

This study addresses the challenge of identifying the nearest negative imaginary framework (NI) when provided with an initial stabilizing controller. It is demonstrated that if the initial controller stabilizes a given linear, time-invariant (LTI) system, the resulting nearest NI framework remains stable. Furthermore, when the initial controller ensures strict stability, the resulting framework exhibits a minimum degree of relative stability. The paper also presents a specific algorithm for locating the closest NI system, which is particularly useful for controller design. Numerical examples are included to validate these findings.

Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems are typically trained on a fixed dataset and then evaluated against a separate test set. However, in real-world scenarios, these systems must handle a continuous stream of new data, necessitating the ability to learn from new information without forgetting previously acquired knowledge. This paper investigates continual learning strategies specifically for automatic speech recognition, focusing on the prevention of catastrophic forgetting. We introduce a continual learning framework designed to train a single ASR model on a sequence of non-overlapping datasets. Our approach employs a replay mechanism that utilizes a limited pool of previously seen samples to refresh the model's parameters during training on new data. Experiments conducted on the TIMIT corpus demonstrate that this method effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting, with performance on older tasks remaining comparable to models trained on all data simultaneously.

Code-switching, the alternation between two or more languages within a single sentence, is a prevalent linguistic phenomenon. This paper details the sentiment analysis approach we developed for our team's entry in the SemEval-2020 Task 9, which focused on identifying sentiment in code-switching text. Our methodology employed a deep learning model to analyze the submitted dataset, which consisted of 1,000 sentences in a Spanish-English mix. Our team secured the 10th place ranking on the challenge's final evaluation set.

This study explores a low-scale leptogenesis scenario within a framework featuring a Higgs doublet, a triplet, and a scalar singlet, where the latter mediates seesaw dynamics via three-loop radiative corrections. We analyze how the scalar singlet's mass influences the relic density of dark matter, identifying a specific parameter region where low-scale leptogenesis and dark matter phenomenology mutually reinforce each other.

This study introduces a novel neural network architecture designed to predict user responses by leveraging item characteristics. The proposed model utilizes a new item embedding layer that constructs item representations based on co-occurrence patterns within a specific dataset. The authors evaluate this approach on a real-world dataset from a major e-commerce platform, where users assess products on a five-star scale. The results demonstrate that the new method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy.

This study introduces a robust joint design for transceiver optimization in IRS-assisted, cell-free networks, specifically addressing the adverse effects of channel estimation errors. The primary goal is to maximize the minimum achievable data rate across all users by incorporating these estimation inaccuracies. To achieve this, we formulate the problem as a non-convex quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP) and employ a semidefinite relaxation (SDR) approach. Subsequently, we apply the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to decompose the resulting SDP into simpler subproblems that can be solved efficiently. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that the proposed robust design significantly outperforms existing benchmark methods in terms of minimum user rate, particularly under severe channel estimation error conditions.

Branch prediction is a critical component of modern processors, and Dynamic Branch Prediction (DBP) has emerged as a promising avenue for enhancing branch prediction accuracy by leveraging historical program execution patterns. This survey offers a comprehensive overview of recent deep learning techniques applied to DBP. The work begins by detailing the fundamental principles of traditional DBP approaches, followed by an examination of how deep learning architectures have been employed to address various DBP challenges. The analysis covers the utilization of diverse neural network models, the specific input data features these models process, and the metrics used to evaluate prediction accuracy. Finally, the survey identifies key unresolved issues and potential future research trajectories within the field of deep learning for dynamic branch prediction.

Active visual control is a critical component of autonomous systems, particularly for tasks like autonomous driving, where it is essential to determine optimal camera settings. This paper introduces a deep convolutional neural network designed to predict the best camera orientation given a specific target object and its current pose. The proposed method employs imitation learning, training the network on data derived from an expert controller that selects the ideal viewing angle. This expert is modeled using a utility function that balances the target object's size and its position within the frame. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 10% improvement in performance.

This paper investigates the one-dimensional SOS model featuring a three-spin interaction, demonstrating that its resulting partition function satisfies a specific second-order difference equation with a non-linear structure. Furthermore, we derive the corresponding product formula for this partition function, alongside explicit expressions for the SOS model's Gibbs measures.

This study introduces a novel approach to resonance power transfer (RPT) utilizing an entangled photon pair, where the donor and acceptor are positioned within an arbitrary medium. We demonstrate that the entanglement between the photons enables the donor to sense the resonance condition of the acceptor even when they are spatially separated. Consequently, this method allows for the achievement of RPT without the donor and acceptor needing to share a common resonant frequency, offering significant potential for advancing quantum information processing within nonlinear optical environments.

This study investigates the robustness of coupling constants for charmed and bottom mesons relative to light vector mesons by employing QCD sum rules. Specifically, we examine the correlation between the coupling constant of the $B_{(c)}^*$ meson and the $B_{(c)}$ meson, alongside the relationship between the decay constants of the $B_{(c)}^*$ meson and $\rho$ meson. Our findings indicate that these coupling constants exhibit significant variation with respect to the mass of the light vector mesons, suggesting that the QCD sum rule method is not highly reliable for determining these values.

This document outlines the experimental initiatives planned for neutrinos in the coming years. It details the objectives, underlying physics, and current status of these projects, specifically examining long-baseline accelerator experiments, reactor-based studies, searches for neutrinoless double-beta decay, environmental neutrino observations, and the upcoming generation of accelerator-based experiments.

This paper examines the causal impact of continuous variables, utilizing linear regression models to estimate the marginal per-unit effects of covariates on an outcome. We demonstrate that, under the assumption of linear structural equations, these regression coefficients correspond to the derivatives of a specific class of causal functionals. This correspondence holds regardless of whether the data is pooled across different treatment levels or stratified. Crucially, these identified functionals are robust to unobserved confounding provided that such confounding is conditionally independent of covariates given observed variables. Consequently, these functionals are identified within a broad range of causal models, including those where the effect of a covariate is invariant across all treatments. We further establish that these functionals are generally unidentified only when treatment effects vary depending on the treatment status.

This paper introduces a novel damping controller for wide-area power oscillations, designed exclusively for a controlled interline power (VSC) within a point-of-interconnection (POI) context. By leveraging data from Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs), the proposed controller is established on a model-free framework utilizing a data-driven approach. The methodology employs a two-stage Least Squares Support Vector Regression (LSSVR) algorithm to forecast the post-fault dynamics of VSC active power and the relevant PMU measurements. Subsequently, a model-free damping controller is formulated based on these predictions. The controller's efficacy is validated through simulations on a two-area test system, demonstrating its superiority over conventional wide-area controllers.

We introduce a two-atom system where the interaction is mediated by a common optical cavity, and we demonstrate that the subradiant steady state is governed by the decay of superradiant states. This conclusion is reached by analyzing the two-atom density matrix under the rotating wave approximation, and it is further shown that the subradiant population increases as the interatomic distance grows.

This study examines the long-term dynamics of a kink in a nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation featuring a double-well potential, subject to two distinct perturbations: an internal mode excitation and an external force. By employing a decomposition method, we separate the kink into its constituent parts—an intrinsic kink component and components projected onto a set of orthogonal functions. We establish that, provided the initial conditions satisfy a specific constraint, the kink configuration remains asymptotically stable despite these unusual perturbation factors.

The text details the research program for hadron physics at J-PARC, highlighting that the study of color transparency is central to it. It outlines how the facility's extensive energy spectrum and broad range of beam intensities enable diverse experimental approaches, from high-energy studies at Hadron Super Ring (HSR) to those at medium-energy rings. Specific experiments are described, including the measurement of the nuclear transparency of $\pi^+$ and $K^-$ beams at HSR, the investigation of the nuclear transparency of $\pi^0$ and $K^-$ beams at J-PARC Energy Beam Line (EBL), and the analysis of the nuclear transparency of $\pi^0$ mesons at HSR. Additionally, the text explains that upcoming experiments will utilize the HSR to examine the nuclear transparency of $K^-$ and $K^0$ mesons, as well as the J-PARC J-PARC Energy Beam Line (EBL) to study the nuclear transparency of $\pi^0$ and $K^-$ beams. The text concludes by noting that the nuclear transparency of $\pi^0$ and $K^-$ beams at HSR will be studied using the J-PARC Energy Beam Line (EBL).

Consistency training has recently emerged as a promising approach for unsupervised pre-training, leveraging the principle that minor input perturbations should yield outputs similar to the original input. While this method has demonstrated strong performance, its reliance on the model's current predictions to generate perturbations introduces a critical limitation: the approach is prone to collapsing into a trivial solution where the model merely replicates its initial predictions. To address this, we introduce Consistency Training with Virtual Adversarial Discrete Disturbance (CVDD). CVDD generates perturbations using a predefined discrete distribution, thereby eliminating the need for explicit feature representations and predictions. This design not only enhances training efficiency but also significantly improves generalization. Empirical results confirm that CVDD surpasses existing state-of-the-art consistency training methods, achieving superior performance on the ImageNet-10% benchmark.

Detecting polyps in endoscopic videos is crucial for identifying colorectal cancer. While deep learning has become the standard for such detection, current methods often struggle with low accuracy due to the scarcity of annotated data and the high variability in polyp appearances. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel spatio-temporal feature transformation (STFT) module designed to enhance the performance of multi-frame polyp detection. The STFT module leverages a multi-frame approach to extract more comprehensive features by integrating spatial and temporal information. Specifically, it employs a dedicated spatio-temporal feature transformation (STFT) module to convert the spatial features of the first frame into richer temporal representations. These transformed features are then fused with the original spatial features to create a comprehensive representation that captures both dimensions. The STFT module further utilizes a specialized temporal attention mechanism to weigh the importance of subsequent frames, allowing the model to focus on the most informative temporal data. Experimental results demonstrate that this STFT module significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 2.5% increase in mAP on the Kvasir-CT dataset. The source code is available at https://github.com/chenyuan1996/STFT-Detection.

Stream sampling is a critical technique in environmental research, yet it faces significant hurdles, particularly when dealing with spatially and temporally unevenly distributed data points. To address these issues, we introduce a method for generating spatially balanced sample sets from streams, even when data collection intervals vary. This approach employs a Markov chain Monte Carlo framework, utilizing a novel, computationally efficient proposal distribution that ensures rapid convergence to the target. Furthermore, we develop an algorithm for assessing the statistical significance of trends in water quality metrics. This algorithm integrates a robust non-parametric test with a multiple testing correction to handle the temporal dependencies inherent in stream monitoring. We validate our approach using both simulated datasets and real-world stream monitoring data.

The $rp$-process occurring in the rapid proton capture ($rp$) chain of type I X-ray bursts (XBFs) is heavily influenced by the nuclear abundances of $^{56}$Ni and $^{57}$Zn. This study presents the first measurement of the $\beta$-delayed proton emission branching ratio for $^{57}$Zn, yielding a value of $P_{p} = (1.0 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-3}$. This result is consistent with prior estimates and indicates that the abundance of $^{57}$Zn is sufficient to prevent the $rp$-process from stalling at $^{56}$Ni. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that the $rp$-process can proceed effectively through $^{57}$Zn, bypassing the potential bottleneck at $^{56}$Ni.

This paper investigates the Manin-Mumford conjecture within number field elliptic curves defined over parameter fields using the framework of dynamical systems. We establish that for a generic point of infinite order on such curves, torsion points within the fibers of the parameter space form a finite set. Furthermore, we prove that torsion points are bounded by the fibers of the map. These findings rely on the techniques of height functions and dynamical systems.

This study reports on the analysis of Very High Energy (VHE) gamma-ray emission from 14 pulsars located in the Northern Hemisphere, utilizing data from the VERITAS telescope array. The investigation focused on the pulsars' immediate surroundings, searching for evidence of gamma-ray radiation. The dataset comprises 10.6 to 20.6 years of observations, with an average exposure of 15.5 years. The analysis employed a novel method to identify extended emission, involving the subtraction of the Point Source Search (PSS) likelihood map from the total field map. The resulting residuals were then compared against simulated images of known pulsar nebulae. The study found no significant evidence for extended emission in the vicinity of any of the observed pulsars. Consequently, the paper establishes upper limits on the flux of extended emission, which are notably more stringent than previous findings.

This study investigates the long-term asymptotic behavior of solutions to a reaction-diffusion equation featuring nonlocal boundary conditions, defined on the boundary of a bounded domain whose boundary possesses fractal characteristics. We establish that the associated global attractor exhibits a finite fractal dimension under a specific Hausdorff measure characterized by a dimension strictly less than $n-1/2$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this attractor is weakly fractal, indicating that it contracts the boundary's fractal nature while maintaining its invariance under the dynamics.

We introduce a machine learning framework designed to identify extragalactic Ultra-Compact Dwarfs (UCDs) and Globular Groups (GGs) within the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) database. This method leverages the morphological and photometric characteristics of UCDs and GGs, which are typically found in the central regions of galaxies. To enhance the interpretability of the model's decisions, we utilize SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to isolate the most critical features for classification. Our analysis reveals that the concentration of light in the central galaxy, the galaxy's total luminosity, and the galaxy's color are the primary drivers in distinguishing UCDs and GGs from other galaxy types. Furthermore, we present a novel, refined classification scheme for UCDs and GGs based on these morphological and photometric parameters. Applying this scheme to the SDSS data, we identified 1,001 UCDs and 1,001 GGs, with the latter being 1,001 times more numerous than the former.

Suggestion systems are ubiquitous across various domains, including e-commerce, social networking, and recruitment. Although the literature offers extensive research on developing these systems, there is a notable lack of work addressing the strategic decision-making processes required to deploy them effectively in a business setting. This paper presents an industry-centric perspective on the decisions involved in implementing suggestion systems. It outlines the essential components of such systems, the methodology for assessing their value, and the specific challenges encountered during deployment. Furthermore, the authors illustrate these concepts with a practical case study from an industry context.

This paper addresses the challenge of testing the mean of a population with a finite but finite support, where the underlying distribution is characterized by an infinite right tail. Such distributions are classified as extremely heavy-tailed. In these scenarios, the sample mean is an inefficient estimator of the population parameter, and the standard Central Limit Theorem fails to apply. To address this, we introduce a new test statistic based on the truncated sample mean. We establish the asymptotic behavior of this statistic and demonstrate its consistency. We further evaluate the test's finite-sample performance through Monte Carlo simulations and illustrate its practical application using real-world datasets.

Motor Imagery Brain-Computer Interface (MI-BCI) systems are increasingly utilized for controlling assistive devices, yet their effectiveness is often hindered by low signal quality and signal variability. To address this, we introduce a new Sinc-based Convolutional Neural Network (SCNN) designed to enhance the classification of MI-BCI data. The SCNN framework integrates a specialized Sinc filter bank with a learnable convolutional layer, enabling it to capture both local and global features from raw MI-BCI signals. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SCNN outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in MI-BCI classification tasks.

In this study, we introduce a consistent quantization framework for the fermionic sector of the noncommutative $AdS_2$ model. By employing the corresponding mode expansion for the noncommutative spinor field, we establish a mapping between this noncommutative sector and an equivalent quantized fermionic theory on commutative $AdS_2$. We demonstrate that this mapping preserves the essential features of the theory, including the Dirac equation and the underlying $Sp(2,R)$ symmetry. Furthermore, we confirm that the Dirac propagator for the noncommutative model can be derived directly from the Dirac propagator of the commutative model via this correspondence.

Kidney transplant recipients derive significant benefits from extended donor kidneys, yet these organs often exhibit lower quality than ideal. This study introduces a mathematical framework to determine the optimal policy for accepting unmatched kidneys, with the goal of maximizing total patient-years. The model accounts for the variability in post-transplant survival and waiting times, which fluctuate based on individual patient characteristics and donor organ status. By applying dynamic programming, we demonstrate that an optimal acceptance threshold exists, defined by a patient's pre-transplant survival probability. Furthermore, we analyze how this ideal acceptance threshold shifts in response to changes in the waiting list population.

This study introduces a novel hybridization approach combining Hidden Markov Models (HMM) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to enhance the performance of both individual models. The proposed method leverages the temporal dependencies of HMMs and the long-term memory capabilities of LSTMs. To achieve this, the HMM is trained to generate the LSTM's input sequences, while the LSTM's hidden state outputs are utilized to train the HMM. Experimental results demonstrate that this integrated model outperforms standalone HMM and LSTM architectures in terms of accuracy.

This paper investigates the boundedness and compactness properties of the generalized Volterra integral operator acting on biased Bergman spaces. We establish a criterion for the boundedness of this operator in terms of specific norms of the biased Bergman spaces and demonstrate that it corresponds to half of a bounded Toeplitz operator on the same spaces.

We introduce a novel method for simultaneously compressing multiple cross-lingual models, which we term joint pruning. This approach involves training a single, unified architecture to handle multiple tasks, allowing for shared pruning masks across the entire model. We evaluate our technique on two sets of multilingual job functions: (1) multilingual machine translation (MT) and (2) multilingual question answering (QA). Our findings indicate that the joint model achieves performance comparable to individually trained models while reducing the total parameter count by 50%. Additionally, we demonstrate that the joint model requires 2.5 fewer FLOPs per inference operation than its individually trained counterparts.

The surge in data-driven artificial intelligence has sparked a corresponding rise in the volume and variety of available data. This paper offers a concise review of the primary data repositories and their access protocols, highlighting the critical challenges and promising opportunities within the data science community. The piece concludes by briefly addressing the ethical and legal complexities surrounding data usage.

This paper examines decomposable Richelot isogenies applied to the Jacobians of hyperelliptic curves. We present a generalized Riemann-Hurwitz type hyperelliptic curve that supports such isogenies, which in turn induces a generalized Richelot isogeny on the curves' Jacobians. This generalized construction serves as an extension of the generalized Howe isogeny found in low-genus cases.

We introduce a method for estimating positive semi-definite (PSD) symmetric matrices with a fixed rank $r$ from noisy observations of selected entries. This approach utilizes Gaussian elimination to derive a system of linear equations, which is subsequently resolved using volume sampling. Theoretically, we demonstrate that the proposed estimator achieves a mean squared error (MSE) bounded by $O(r^2md^2/\epsilon^2)$, where $m$ represents the sample size, $d$ is the dimension, and $\epsilon$ denotes the noise level. Notably, this estimator matches the optimal sample complexity of $O(md/\epsilon^2)$ established by prior work on low-rank PSD estimation, while offering the advantage of being computationally efficient.

This work introduces a comprehensive collection of revision histories for all articles in the English Wikipedia, available via **http://www.wikihist.html.wikihistory.org/wiki/{article}**. The provided HTML is specifically designed for human readers, yet it includes a full-text representation suitable for computational analysis. This resource serves as a valuable tool for investigating collaborative writing processes and acts as an open-data repository for research into the evolution of Wikipedia content.

Twisted bilayers of magnetic materials offer a versatile framework for investigating emergent phenomena, including quantum spin liquids and topological textures. This study examines the ground states of twisted bilayers composed of two distinct magnetic materials, characterized by a lattice of merons and antimerons. We demonstrate that these lattices exhibit a polar nature, with spontaneous spin-polarization oriented perpendicular to the bilayer plane. Furthermore, we explore the potential for manipulating these spin-polarizations through external magnetic fields and strain, which can induce transitions between different ground states. These findings underscore the significance of twisted bilayers in the search for novel magnetic phases and topological matter.

This study examines the influence of cosmic expansion on the spacetime interval between two observers, a phenomenon that becomes relevant when the interval's magnitude approaches the universe's scale. We demonstrate that for observers comoving with the cosmic flow, this expansion induces a time dilation effect, whereas spatial components of the interval remain unaffected by expansion. Consequently, redshift is not merely a spectral shift but a fundamental alteration of the time interval between such observers. We argue that the expansion of the universe is therefore not a uniform stretching of all spatial and temporal dimensions, but specifically a dilation of the intervals between observers who share the cosmic frame.

We demonstrate that colloidal particles can be guided along pre-defined routes within nematic liquid crystals confined by wave-like structures. The interaction between the colloids and the liquid crystal is mediated by the surface's geometry, which imposes a specific periodicity on the material's alignment. This pattern generates corresponding gradients in the local director orientation, establishing a potential energy landscape that features parallel ridges and valleys. By applying an external magnetic field, these ridges can be selectively strengthened or weakened, thereby allowing precise control over the direction of the resulting particle motion.

This study examines how a planet's close approach affects a rubble-pile asteroid, specifically analyzing the sensitivity of its surface to tidal forces. We demonstrate that the degree of surface disruption depends on both the planet-asteroid distance and the asteroid's elongation. Specifically, the tidal acceleration experienced at the surface is directly proportional to the planet's mass and the asteroid's elongation, while being inversely proportional to the cube of the planet-asteroid separation. Consequently, the surface sensitivity is markedly higher for elongated asteroids compared to spherical ones. These findings are quantified by introducing a dimensionless parameter, $\mathcal{S}$, representing asteroid surface sensitivity. We establish that asteroids with $\mathcal{S} \geq 1$ are prone to significant surface deformation during encounters. Furthermore, we identify a critical distance, $r_{\rm crit}$, below which such bodies undergo substantial changes. This critical distance is inversely proportional to the asteroid's density and elongation, and directly proportional to the planet's mass. Finally, we apply these results to the 2012 DA4 asteroid, showing that its surface sensitivity during a 2029 encounter with Earth is minimal.

Simulating molecular dynamics is a crucial task for quantum chemistry, yet it is often hindered by the scarcity of rare events, such as protein folding or conformational changes. While traditional methods like umbrella sampling and parallel replica dynamics can enhance sampling efficiency, they frequently fail to capture the full complexity of these rare transitions. This paper introduces a new quantum algorithm designed to estimate the probability of rare events within quantum systems. By employing quantum amplitude estimation, the algorithm achieves a quadratic improvement in computational complexity compared to classical Monte Carlo methods. We demonstrate the utility of this approach through two case studies: simulating the structural rearrangement of a small peptide and modeling the dynamics of a quantum spin system.

We introduce MAPPIES, a novel Monte-Carlo code designed to simulate the radiative processes of a relativistic electron traversing an external radiation field. This code accounts for the effects of a partially polarized external field, incorporating inverse Compton scattering, synchrotron emission, and pair production. The resulting energy spectra and polarization characteristics of the emitted radiation are derived from an ensemble of randomly distributed and polarized electrons. We present initial results for inverse Compton scattering, demonstrating that the code successfully replicates established analytical solutions for both fully polarized and unpolarized external fields. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of varying external field parameters on the resulting photon spectra and polarization. Finally, we apply this code to model the broadband spectrum of the blazar TXS 0506+056, yielding a preliminary fit that aligns well with observational data.

The Arctic Ocean's sea ice thickness distribution (SITD) is a critical indicator of ice conditions, yet its evolution remains poorly understood. This study utilizes a 20-year dataset of satellite-derived SITD to investigate its seasonal development. The analysis reveals that the distribution's development is not uniform across all regions; instead, it is governed by the interaction between the ice-ocean interface and the ice-ice interface. Specifically, the ice-ocean interface dictates the distribution's shape, while the ice-ice interface controls its migration. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that the distribution can be effectively described using a single parameter, which is determined by the average thickness of the ice.

We investigate the Weierstrass semigroups at multiple points, denoted $W(P,Q)$ on two points $P,Q$, and $W(P_1,\dots,P_r)$ at a collection of points on specific maximal curves of genus $g=3n^2-n+n$ and $g=n(n-1)+3$ respectively. These structures generalize the Hermitian case. Our approach involves a two-step process: first, we determine $W(P,Q)$ for the curves of genus $g=3n^2-n+n$ by utilizing their construction as quotients of $A^2$ by an additive group, and second, we derive $W(P_1,\dots,P_r)$ for the curves of genus $g=n(n-1)+3$ by relating them to a quotient of the former curves by an involution.

Singing Voice Synthesis (SVS) represents a specialized subfield of speech processing that generates synthetic audio by mapping lyrics and musical notation to corresponding vocals. While traditional approaches relied on blending pre-recorded audio segments, recent advancements in deep learning have enabled the creation of highly realistic, lifelike audio from textual and notational inputs. This survey offers a comprehensive review of current deep learning-based SVS architectures, examining their underlying principles, specific methodologies, and performance metrics. Additionally, we discuss critical evaluation techniques, highlight existing limitations, and explore promising avenues for future research.

We introduce NIPS4Bplus, a comprehensive dataset comprising 1,000 bird species, which has been significantly expanded to include over 10,000 sound recordings. This dataset features extensive annotations, encompassing species names, specific calls, recording locations, and environmental contexts. It also offers a unique, detailed breakdown of acoustic properties, such as frequency spectra, waveforms, and duration. To support the development of bird sound analysis tools, we have developed and released a suite of baseline machine learning models, including classifiers for species identification, call typology, and habitat classification.

Event cameras offer significant advantages over conventional frame-based cameras, including high temporal resolution, low latency, and power efficiency. However, the raw event data is difficult to utilize directly due to its asynchronous, sparse, and irregular nature. To address this, event adjustment techniques have been developed to transform event data into frame-like images, thereby enabling the use of existing frame-based computer vision algorithms. Despite this, event adjustment remains a challenging task due to the inherent characteristics of event data. This paper provides a comprehensive review of event adjustment methods, categorizing them into three primary types: image reconstruction, image subtraction, and image fusion. We evaluate these techniques by analyzing their respective advantages and limitations, and we discuss the specific challenges associated with event adjustment. Furthermore, we propose a novel framework that integrates multiple existing methods to overcome these challenges. Finally, we outline several promising future research directions in this field.

Graphs serve as a fundamental data structure for representing diverse real-world entities and their interconnections. In recent years, graph analysis has garnered significant attention across numerous fields, including social networks, knowledge graphs, and bioinformatics. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of graph analysis, encompassing both classical methodologies and cutting-edge developments. We begin by defining the core concepts of graph analysis and introducing essential data structures and algorithms. Subsequently, we examine a wide array of analysis techniques, ranging from basic centrality metrics and clustering coefficients to advanced community detection, node embedding, and graph neural networks. Furthermore, we outline promising future research avenues, such as leveraging large language models for graph reasoning, constructing graphs from text, and addressing ethical challenges like bias and privacy. This survey serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners seeking to deepen their understanding of graph analysis and its practical applications.

This study examines the compilation of arbitrary unitary operations on a single qubit into sequences of $\pi/8$ gates and Hadamard gates, subject to a uniform error bound defined by $\varepsilon$. The analysis reveals two distinct categories of unitary operations, termed "ordinary" and "exceptional," each possessing unique compilation characteristics. For ordinary operations, the minimal number of required $\pi/8$ gates is constant at 2, regardless of how small $\varepsilon$ becomes. Conversely, for exceptional operations, the necessary count of $\pi/8$ gates is unbounded as $\varepsilon$ approaches zero. The set of exceptional operations is identified as those unitaries that cannot be decomposed into combinations of the identity operation and Hadamard gates, along with their specific rotations by $\pi/8$ or $-\pi/8$.

This paper introduces a method for 3D instrument tracking during retinal surgery, utilizing a spotlight to project a light spot onto the retina. This projected spot is captured by a camera, which feeds into a deep learning model to estimate the spot's 2D position. By combining this 2D data with the known camera and spotlight geometry, the system calculates the 3D position of the instrument. Furthermore, the paper presents a novel dataset specifically designed for spotlight-assisted retinal surgery guidance, featuring 3D ground truth derived from this surgery setup. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a tracking error of 1.6 mm, with a computational time of 1.2 ms per frame.

This approach offers several advantages, including the ability to estimate the EoR 21-cm signal's amplitude and redshift, as well as the capability to handle complex calibration errors. Furthermore, the method can be applied to data from various EoR experiments.

This work examines the relationship between the quantum cohomology of a smooth projective variety and that of its projectivization, extending these findings to collections of such objects. We introduce a novel deformation of the Hilbert-Chow morphism, termed the projective bundle morphism, which establishes an isomorphism between the quantum cohomology of a projective collection and the corresponding structure of the underlying object. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this new structure serves as a deformation of the pullback from the target's quantum cohomology, thereby generalizing the established result regarding the symplectic structure on $\mathbb{P}(E)$.

This study introduces a novel, highly consistent formulation of prime number theorems. By utilizing the summation of a specific periodic function over intervals defined by the logarithmic function, it establishes an approximation for the count of prime numbers within those ranges. Additionally, an approximation for the prime-counting function, denoted as $\pi(x)$, is derived through the use of complex trigonometric functions.

This paper introduces a statistical methodology designed to analyze Alzheimer's disease clinical trials, specifically targeting the identification of the optimal dosage for a new therapeutic agent. The approach utilizes natural cubic splines to model the relationship between treatment dose and clinical outcomes, with the primary goal of selecting the most effective dose. By integrating these splines with a step-down multiple testing procedure, the method offers a statistically rigorous framework for dose selection. The performance of this proposed approach is validated through a simulation study, and its practical applicability is demonstrated using data from a real-world Alzheimer's trial.

This paper introduces a novel parking system designed for urban environments, where the primary goal is to enhance the efficiency of the parking process. To achieve this, the proposed system utilizes a tire-mounted sensor to detect parking events, which are subsequently processed through a filtering mechanism to eliminate false positives. Furthermore, a crowdsourcing approach is implemented to manage parking availability data.

Adversarial training is widely regarded as a robust defense against adversarial attacks, yet it often suffers from performance degradation on clean data. This study examines the relationship between adversarial training and the level minima optimization problem. We demonstrate that under specific conditions, the level minima optimization framework can replicate the behavior of adversarial training. Furthermore, it is proven that the level minima objective function is non-convex, and under particular circumstances, it presents a significantly simpler optimization landscape compared to standard adversarial training. To address these conditions, we introduce a new algorithm called Adversarial Level Minimization (ALM). Experimental results indicate that ALM surpasses adversarial training in terms of both robustness and efficiency in terms of training speed.

This paper introduces a reflective parametric frequency selective attenuator (PFA) utilizing Josephson junctions to generate a high-Q comb of notches within a transmission line. By employing a parametric pump, the design achieves a fully tunable notch spectrum with sub-milliwatt power requirements and a loss factor below one decibel.

This study introduces a novel SEIRS epidemiological framework designed to analyze the COVID-19 scenario where recovered individuals retain no acquired immunity. The model examines the dynamic interactions between susceptible, exposed, infectious, and recovered populations, with the infectious compartment subdivided into those who can transmit the virus and those who cannot. The core contribution is the derivation of a basic reproduction number, denoted as $\mathcal{R}_0$, which serves as a threshold for determining whether the disease-free equilibrium is stable. The authors establish the global stability of this equilibrium and demonstrate the existence of an endemic equilibrium point, further proving its stability under specific conditions. The theoretical findings are corroborated by numerical simulations.

This paper investigates the impact of context window size on word embedding quality. We evaluate various window sizes across multiple benchmark tasks, including word similarity, analogy solving, and word clustering. Our findings indicate that a window size of 4 to 6 words is optimal for the EMBEDDING_CORRECTED model, outperforming both smaller and larger windows. While a wider context of up to 20 words yields results comparable to this optimum, performance degrades when the window size is significantly increased.

This study examines the maximum size of $k$-cliques within the context of high-intensity, $(d+1)$-dimensional, Poissonian random geometric graphs. We establish a rigorous lower bound for this parameter, which aligns with the corresponding upper bound originally proposed by Penrose. Specifically, when $d=1$, our derived lower bound improves upon a finding by Frieze et al.

We introduce a Lagrangian framework for studying rotating stars, derived from a fluid action that incorporates a Lagrange multiplier to enforce the constraint of incompressibility. This formalism enables the calculation of equilibrium configurations for rotating stars, yielding the Lagrangian counterpart to the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the angular momentum per particle remains constant throughout the Lagrangian evolution, which aligns with the standard understanding of irrotational flow under Kepler's law.

The Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) model serves as a significant solution to Einstein's field equations, representing an inhomogeneous, spherically symmetric distribution of pressureless matter. This study extends the LTB framework to General Relativity within Palatini $f(R)$ gravity, deriving the resulting metric and its associated Ricci tensor. We demonstrate that the generalized equation of motion for the scale factor $R(t,r)$ adheres to the original form found in General Relativity's LTB solution. Furthermore, we establish that the proper radius and proper time within this generalized model retain the same functional forms as those in the standard LTB case.

Quantum nonlocality serves as a fundamental resource for various quantum information processing tasks. This study demonstrates that quantum nonlocality can be robustly realized in $N$-partite systems composed of $N$ qubits, even under significant noise conditions. We introduce a class of $N$-partite quantum states that exhibit robust quantum nonlocality, defined by the property that the probability of violating Bell inequalities remains constant regardless of the magnitude of the noise. This robustness stems from the specific structure of these states, which are constructed using a tensor product of $N$-dimensional generalized Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states. We further establish that this state structure is both necessary and sufficient for achieving robust quantum nonlocality. Additionally, we demonstrate that these states possess robust quantum correlations, which can be verified through the violation of Bell-type correlation inequalities.

This study introduces a novel approach for forecasting human visual attention in web pages by leveraging gaze data analytics. The method utilizes gaze metrics to construct a feature set that captures the interdependencies among eye-tracking signals, which are subsequently modeled using a continuous-time Markov chain. The resulting output provides a forward-looking estimation of attention metrics for brief durations. The model's effectiveness was validated against a dataset comprising 100 recorded eye-tracking sessions from users interacting with Wikipedia articles.

This paper introduces a novel transmission reconfigurable intelligent surface (TRIS) designed to actively modulate incident electromagnetic waves by dynamically adjusting the phase and amplitude of the transmitted signal. The study details the development of a 16-element TRIS prototype, which is then evaluated through a series of experimental demonstrations. These experiments assess the system's performance in active beamforming, multi-user multi-stream transmission, and beam nulling. The results confirm that the TRIS prototype achieves a high efficiency of 90% in modulating phase and amplitude and can be effectively integrated into 6G communication frameworks.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL) involves learning a policy from a fixed dataset, a scenario that is prevalent in practical applications. While recent research has primarily concentrated on linear-function-approximation-based offline RL, this paper investigates a broader class of offline RL problems using a linear optimization framework combined with linear function approximation. We demonstrate that this framework can effectively address various offline RL challenges, including those involving nonlinearities. Furthermore, we introduce a new algorithm that achieves a regret bound of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{dH})$ for the linear case and $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{dH^2})$ for the nonlinear case, where $d$ represents the dimensionality of the function approximator and $H$ denotes the episode length. These findings improve upon the previously established $\mathcal{O}(d^{1.5}H)$ and $\mathcal{O}(d^{1.5}H^2)$ bounds, respectively.

This paper presents an elementary demonstration that every homotopy equivalence possesses an inverse to function as a homotopy equivalence, with the proof relying on the fact that the space consists of finite complexes. Uniquely, the proof employs the Borel construction and establishes the invertibility via a direct, purely homotopical argument.

We present the first detection of a turbulent supermassive black hole (SMBH) in the distant galaxy J0437+2456. This finding stems from a detailed analysis of the central broad emission line (BLR) of the quasar, which reveals a turbulent velocity dispersion of approximately 1000 km/s. This measurement is significantly lower than the typical velocities observed in other quasar BLRs, suggesting that J0437+2456 is a relatively compact system. Furthermore, the black hole's mass is estimated at $1.1 \times 10^9 M_\odot$, implying a mass-to-light ratio of roughly 0.01. This low ratio indicates that the central black hole dominates the galaxy's mass budget, a characteristic often seen in the most massive elliptical galaxies. The quasar's high luminosity ($L_{\rm bol} \approx 10^{47}$ erg/s) and the turbulent nature of the SMBH suggest that J0437+2456 is a young, rapidly growing system.

This paper examines planar reduced three-body systems where one mass is infinitesimal, focusing specifically on scenarios in which this mass adheres to a straight-line trajectory. We demonstrate that, aside from periodic and periodic-like orbits previously identified by Llibre and Novaes, no further periodic solutions exist for these motions. Conversely, we establish that an abundance of periodic orbits are found when the infinitesimal mass moves along a straight line within the n-body context.

Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) is a non-invasive technique that measures the fluorescence decay of individual molecules, offering a robust method for characterizing their chemical environment. This study introduces a deconvolution approach to enhance the spatial resolution of FLIM images. The technique involves convolving the original FLIM image with a kernel derived from the point spread function (PSF) of the microscope, followed by the application of a Wiener filter to the resulting image. This process effectively reduces the blurring inherent in FLIM data, thereby improving resolution. Furthermore, this method is capable of distinguishing between two closely positioned fluorescent objects, provided they are separated by a distance exceeding the PSF width.

Product search systems are pivotal to e-commerce, yet existing methods often fail to account for the intricate interplay between users and products. To address this, we introduce a graph-based deep learning model designed to capture such complex user-product dynamics. Our approach constructs a heterogeneous graph integrating product metadata and user behavior, utilizing Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) to extract deep representations of these user-product relationships. Additionally, we incorporate a Transformer module to derive comprehensive user profiles. These representations are then employed to generate personalized recommendations for product retrieval. Experimental results demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques in product search scenarios.

Graph data, characterized by nodes and their interconnections, is prevalent across numerous domains. While prior research has primarily focused on supervised learning scenarios involving graph data, real-world applications often demand unsupervised learning when node labels are absent. This paper introduces a novel approach for embedding graph data in an unsupervised context. The proposed method constructs a deep manifold labeled graph (DMLG) that integrates both the structural topology and node attributes. It subsequently generates a low-dimensional representation by jointly optimizing the manifold and the embedding through a unified objective function. Theoretical analysis confirms that the resulting embedding problem is convex. Furthermore, extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that the method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This paper introduces a novel method for designing non-orthogonal sequences within grant-free massive connectivity frameworks. The core strategy involves generating binary non-equidistant sequences with balanced Hamming weights, which are subsequently transformed into complex-valued sequences with unit magnitude through a two-stage evolutionary process. The initial stage employs genetic algorithms to optimize sequence Hamming distances, followed by a second stage utilizing genetic algorithms to adjust sequence phases while maintaining their Hamming weights. This approach is designed to maximize the minimum distance between any pair of candidate sequences, thereby reducing the probability of sequence ambiguity. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of the minimum distance achieved between sequences.

This study introduces a novel encoder-blind coded sensing framework that employs combinatorial designs for signal acquisition. Unlike conventional sensing methods, which rely on specific restrictions on the sensing matrix to guarantee signal recovery, this proposed approach imposes significantly fewer constraints on both matrix construction and the reconstruction algorithm. By utilizing combinatorial designs, the framework effectively reduces the matrix dimensions and enhances sensing performance. Furthermore, the proposed method allows for the integration of a reconstruction algorithm utilizing both the sensing matrix and the acquired measurements. Numerical simulations demonstrate that this approach achieves superior performance compared to traditional sensing methods.

Domain adaptation seeks to enhance the performance of a model trained on source data for the purpose of classification within a target domain. A primary challenge in this field is the domain shift, which occurs when the source and target distributions differ. While adversarial domain adaptation aims to minimize domain-specific information to create domain-invariant representations, this approach often struggles with overfitting to the source domain. To address this limitation, we introduce a new method that integrates both adversarial and random transformations. This dual approach generates invariant features capable of generalizing across both domains. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed framework outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques on benchmark datasets.

This paper establishes that certain 2-local derivatives on matrix-Jordan algebras defined over commutative involutive rings are, in fact, local derivatives. As a consequence of this result, specific two-sided and local derivatives on corresponding matrix algebras are also derived.

This study investigates the Berry phase of a two-level quantum system where the surrounding environment distorts the geometric nature of the system's parameter space. Specifically, the analysis focuses on scenarios where the actual parameter space is modeled as a Dirac singularity at its core. We demonstrate that when this space is lensed by such a singularity, the resulting Berry phase exhibits a discontinuity. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that the lensing-induced phase discontinuity is governed by the lensing parameters, allowing the Berry phase to be engineered to take on arbitrary values through the lensing of the Dirac singularity.

This study examines the existence of compactons within spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates (SOC-BECs) by employing the sine-Gordon model. We investigate how spin-orbit coupling and the spin-orbit coupling density influence the formation of compactons, revealing that compactons can emerge under both positive and negative values of the spin-orbit coupling parameter. Furthermore, our findings indicate that both spin-orbit coupling and the spin-orbit coupling density affect the spatial extent of compactons, demonstrating that these factors can alter the compacton's width by up to 100%.

The $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$, which decays into $J/\psi \pi^+$, is identified as a $1/2^+$ state within the heavy quark spin symmetry (HQSS) multiplet containing $\Lambda_c(2560)^+$ and $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$, a pair of $3/2^+$ states. This assignment is supported by the HQSS selection rule regarding the decay $\Lambda_c(2595)^+ \to J/\psi \pi^+$, which forbids the decay of the $3/2^+$ $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$ state. However, recent experimental data from BESIII reveal a decay width for $\Lambda_c(2625)^+ \to J/\psi \pi^+$ that is approximately 10% of the width for $\Lambda_c(2595)^+ \to J/\psi \pi^+$. This significant discrepancy challenges the traditional identification of $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$ as the HQSS partner of $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$. This paper investigates the decay $\Lambda_c(2625)^+ \to J/\psi \pi^+$ using a phenomenological model that incorporates HQSS, specifically by treating the decay as a transition between two HQSS multiplets. This paper examines the $C(X)^G$ algebra of continuous functions on a compact metric space $X$ that are invariant under a compact Lie group $G$. We demonstrate that every such $C(X)^G$ algebra can be approximated by $C(Y)^H$ algebras, where $Y$ is a compact metric space and $H$ is a finite subgroup of $G$. Furthermore, we explore the relationship between the algebraic structure of $C(X)^H$ and the topological properties of $C(X)^H$'s spectrum.

This paper outlines the feasibility of detecting heavy, derivative-coupled axion-like particles (ALPs) at future high-energy muon colliders. We examine the potential for identifying ALPs with masses ranging from 10 GeV to 1 TeV, which possess couplings to gluons and photons. Our analysis demonstrates that the muon collider's unique kinematic reach and the distinctive signatures arising from the decay of on-shell ALPs enable the discovery of these particles in regions of the parameter space that are inaccessible to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). Furthermore, we detail the specific experimental capabilities required to achieve these discoveries and provide preliminary estimates of the necessary integrated luminosity for the proposed searches.

Cross-layer optimization involves using data from one layer of a computer system to enhance the performance of another. While this approach has been extensively studied in academia, it remains largely absent from commercial products due to the significant challenges in designing, evaluating, and deploying such systems. To address this gap, we introduce MetaSys, an open-source, practical framework designed to facilitate both the implementation and assessment of cross-layer optimizations. MetaSys integrates metadata from various system layers into a unified, centralized repository, providing a standardized interface for accessing and updating this information. This paper outlines the design and implementation of MetaSys, demonstrates its utility through three specific examples of cross-layer optimizations, and reports on its real-world deployment within the Red Hat Enterprise Virtualization Application Platform.

This study introduces a novel approach to transfer learning that leverages both Siamese networks and synthetic data. The authors present a new transfer learning scheme designed to adapt a pre-trained ResNet-50 model for the classification of a new target dataset. The methodology involves generating synthetic data from the source dataset and subsequently training a Siamese network to map samples from both the source and synthetic domains into a shared feature space. A transfer module is then employed to extract features from this space, which are used to train a classifier for the target dataset. The approach is validated using two distinct datasets: the source is CIFAR-10, while the target comprises a custom dataset of handwritten Arabic numerals. Additionally, the method is evaluated against a second scenario where the source is the larger ImageNet dataset and the target is a custom dataset of handwritten English alphabets. Experimental results indicate that this proposed method outperforms existing transfer learning techniques.

This paper examines a quasilinear elliptic system in $\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N \ge 3$) that includes a sublinear and a semilinear term, both subject to an integral constraint. The primary goal is to establish the existence of unique positive solutions for specific parameter ranges. This achievement relies on an optimal application of the moving plane method, combined with an analysis of the asymptotic behavior of solutions to the corresponding homogeneous system.

Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are a foundational element in deep learning, yet they face significant challenges when processing long sequences due to issues like vanishing gradients and saturation. These problems hinder the network's ability to capture dependencies between distant time steps. To address this, we introduce the Fourier Recurrent Unit (FRU), a novel architecture designed to enhance long-term dependencies by leveraging Fourier series. This approach is particularly effective for modeling periodic patterns, which are prevalent in many real-world applications. We demonstrate that FRUs can be seamlessly integrated into existing RNN frameworks. Empirical evaluations across three standard benchmarks—MNIST, Penn Treebank, and ILSVRC—show that FRUs significantly outperform traditional RNN variants in learning long-term connections.

This paper addresses the challenge of navigating to a target in a Markov Decision Process (MDP) by first formulating it as a two-player zero-sum game. In this framework, a navigation agent competes against an adversary who seeks to obstruct the agent's progress. We establish a theoretical bound on the adversary's optimal strategy and demonstrate that, under specific conditions, this bound can be achieved. Additionally, we introduce a novel algorithm designed to identify the agent's optimal policy. Empirical results indicate that this algorithm performs effectively in complex navigation scenarios.

We introduce a novel method for generating high-brilliance, linearly polarized attosecond electron bunches utilizing dual-wake injection. This approach employs a laser pulse to excite two distinct plasma waves within a gas jet, which serve to inject and subsequently accelerate the beam. The initial plasma wave, driven by a circularly polarized laser, creates a hollow electron beam. A second, linearly polarized laser then excites a second plasma wave to transfer the particles from the hollow into a compact, linearly polarized attosecond bunch. The resulting bunch possesses a high normalized emittance of $10^{-6}$ m rad with an energy spread of 0.1% and a duration of 100 attoseconds. The beam's polarization is oriented along the direction of the second laser's electric field. This technique offers a flexible means to control the beam's energy, charge, and polarization, presenting significant potential for applications in ultrafast electron diffraction and coherent electron diffraction imaging.

The emergence of life is a pivotal event in the universe's history, yet its fundamental nature remains a mystery. While the question of life's origin is a longstanding scientific pursuit, the inquiry into how life evolves and how biological complexity increases has historically been neglected. This paper aims to address these unresolved issues by examining life through an astrophysical lens. We begin by defining life as a self-organizing system that self-replicates and self-optimizes, then explore the concept of entropy reduction as a central theme. We argue that the increase in complexity represents a fundamental aspect of the universe's evolution, proposing that the development of life is a natural extension of this process. We conclude by suggesting that the progression toward higher complexity is a universal trend, with life serving as a key mechanism for this evolution.

This study examines the evolution of open-source software development within the field of climate change investigation, utilizing GitHub as a primary repository. By employing a two-stage AI-driven approach, the research identifies key research areas, tracks their development trajectories, and analyzes the resulting software architectures. The findings reveal a significant surge in climate-related open-source contributions, with a distinct shift from the physical sciences to the social sciences. Additionally, the research highlights a growing emphasis on data science and machine learning, alongside an increasing preference for software modularity. The authors conclude that while AI-assisted research mapping offers valuable insights for evidence-based R&D policy-making, it is subject to specific limitations.

Android, the world's most widely adopted mobile platform, is susceptible to Side-Channel Attacks (SCA) targeting sensitive data such as passwords and API keys. While numerous studies have addressed SCA on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), the execution of native code via the Android Native Development Kit (NDK) remains largely unexplored. This paper introduces ASVAAN, a framework designed to automatically analyze NDK binaries for side-channel vulnerabilities. ASVAAN operates in two phases: first, it automatically generates test cases to stress the target application, and second, it employs machine learning to identify potential SCA vulnerabilities. We successfully demonstrated ASVAAN by analyzing an open-source NDK-based password manager, identifying three previously unknown vulnerabilities.

Blockchain technology has gained significant traction within the cryptocurrency sector, with Ethereum emerging as a leading platform for decentralized applications. This study examines the temporal dynamics of the Ethereum transaction ego network, defined as the set of transactions involving a specific source address and its immediate transaction neighbors. We analyze these networks across diverse labeled categories, including transfers, smart contract interactions, and token exchanges, utilizing a temporal graph framework to assess their structural and topological characteristics. Our findings indicate that while the network's overall architecture remains relatively stable over time, the distribution of labels exhibits marked volatility. Furthermore, we observe that certain labels are more prevalent within specific ego networks, suggesting that transaction types serve as a meaningful indicator of behavioral patterns.

We report on the observation of quantum vibrations in the LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ interface, a phenomenon driven by the collective, periodic expansion and contraction of the electron gas. This behavior is revealed through the emergence of a series of regularly spaced sidebands in the microwave conductivity spectrum, appearing alongside the primary fundamental frequency at approximately 10 GHz and its harmonics. The frequency of these sidebands scales with the square root of the electron density, mirroring the behavior of the fundamental frequency. Furthermore, the sidebands' amplitudes are modulated by the electron density and magnetic field, and they exhibit a phase shift relative to the fundamental response. These findings offer a novel approach for characterizing collective electron dynamics in two-dimensional systems.

This paper explores the computational complexity of linear logic proof search for both Bunched and Pomset logics. It demonstrates that proof search for Pomset logic is PSPACE-complete, whereas for Bunched logic, it is EXPTIME-complete. These findings rely on a new, equivalent formulation of Bunched and Pomset logics as a system of interaction, which allows proof search to be represented as a game.

This study demonstrates the applicability of the pentagon principle within the framework of Ding-Iohara-Miki algebras. Building upon this foundation, we derive a novel set of operator relations characterized by a parameter, which generalize the Heisenberg algebra. Furthermore, we establish a set of bilinear relations by bilocalizing the Heisenberg algebra using parameter-dependent operations. A key result of this work is the proof of the pentagon principle for both the mutated Ding-Iohara-Miki algebras and the parameter-deformed Heisenberg algebra.

We introduce a novel, machine-learning-based technique for estimating photometric redshifts, utilizing compelled photometry across the 0.36–4.5 µm spectrum. This method employs a neural network to derive photometric redshifts for galaxies in the W-CDF-S and ELAIS-S1 fields, leveraging deep NIRACI data from the WFC3/IR camera. The dataset comprises 1.2 million galaxies with spectroscopic redshifts from the Cosmic Evolution Survey (COSMOS), which are used to train the neural network. The resulting photometric redshifts are evaluated against the spectroscopic reference sample, yielding a median absolute error of 0.014 and a 10% failure rate (f<sub>5000W}</f>) for the COSMOS sample. Additionally, the photometric redshifts for the W-CDF-S galaxies are compared against those from the COSMOS sample, revealing a median absolute error of 0.014 and a 10% failure rate (f<1000W}</f>) for the COSMOS sample. The photometric redshifts for the W-CDF-S galaxies are compared against those from the COSMOS sample, revealing a median absolute error of 0.014 and a 10% failure rate (f<1000W}</f>) for the COSMOS sample.
